Raven will challenge missing decisions; adopt genuine judgments as nodes and record reasons for the other findings. Before finishing, repeat with phase=finish and the actual diff. Users do not need to supply paths or a decision list. Create a decision node for a judgment or authorization choice, not a fact you can establish by inspection. Put code and test findings in the relevant decision context with revision, path/line or record/version citations and uncertainty; use facts only for known applicability facts, never inferred authority. Keep static findings and organizational judgment distinct within that context, not as separate approval nodes. Use parent_id and depends_on for actual decision relationships and authorization prerequisites, not an evidence-reading checklist. Choosing a policy, default, compatibility tradeoff or whether to accept uncertain evidence can require a real decision. If no human judgment is needed, do not invent a node just to use Raven: keep the registered task, do the work and checks, read the tree and finish through the normal protocol. Existing open decisions and required follow-ups still need that protocol; this guidance does not clear nodes or grant approval. Kickoff and node writes return their static reading promptly. model_pending means inference is still running; use bridge_wait or bridge_get_tree to read the update. Resume with bridge_start_task(task_id=...). To close an accidental task nobody has answered, use bridge_finish_task(status=abandoned, reason=...). Raven is the canvas for the decisions inside a task. You break the task down; Raven finds out who owns what, what the org already settled, and who has to be asked. People reply in Slack; the web overview and personal Raven accounts are optional. Do not ask the user to maintain an ownership map. For an existing external work-item/source reference, use bridge_lookup_record with its exact repository and known identity fields; resolve ambiguity, read the selected record with bridge_get_record, then call bridge_link_work_item with its exact current record/version and canonical identity to attach it to the task. Lookup and reading alone create no association. A structured facts.work_item ID remains visibly unlinked until explicitly attached; context, client_ref and client_key prose never create links. No reimport is needed. These task associations never support or approve a decision; use source_evidence separately for actual premises. Use bridge_connection_status to check connected sources and Slack. Ingest a local checkout when permitted, and import relevant tickets or documents obtained through your connected tools with bridge_import_record. Slack Real-time Search results are transient context, not records to import. 1. Call bridge_start_task the moment a task is kicked off, before any work, with the task as given, the repository, who kicked it off if known (requester), and a client_key of your own so a retry returns the same task. Paths are optional: discover them yourself in the repository; do not ask the user to supply file paths, owners, or a decision list. It returns engage or pass with the reason. On pass, proceed without Raven (still add a node if a real decision appears). It returns unplaced when the task's words name no area and you gave no paths: find the files first, then call bridge_start_task again with the same title, repo and client_key and those files as paths, before your first edit. 2. On engage, write each decision you discover as a node with bridge_add_node, with parent_id set to the decision it grew from; give client_ref so a retry is idempotent, and name in the context the customer, account or case the decision is about. Changed facts on an add retry are not applied: read the current fact_revision and use bridge_correct_node_facts for an explicit complete replacement before human approval. Kickoff candidates are prompts, not a required list of new nodes. Read the existing questions and the current parent answer in bridge_get_tree before adding overlapping questions; add only decisions not already covered in their actual scope. A node's parent context is not authorization for that node or an ownership transfer. A node comes back resolved (evidence from records or signed answers, with a citation, marked for sign-off by the person the signals name), predicted (an unconfirmed default or an unsigned earlier answer), pending (routed to the person the signals name, waiting), unrouted (Raven does not know), or duplicate (the same open decision elsewhere; read through to it). 3. Use bridge_settle_node for your own proposal; when it relies on records you read, pass their exact current source_evidence pins. Prose citations create no links, and existing dependencies stay attached. Omit pins for an unsupported manual opinion. Your proposal supersedes a pending model read but still needs human sign-off; use bridge_wait rather than treating settlement as approval. 4. Evidence is not authorization. Read the current node's authorized and signoff fields. A valid explicit standing grant can authorize a matching node with signoff=rule without a new signature, subject to its current conditions, scope, expiry, source freshness and the existing workspace policy. Historical answer/rationale text describes its original task; a later grant's recorded terms govern conditional reuse. Never infer missing customer, environment or other business facts from that history. A node that remains unauthorized still needs review: prepare on it, do not ship on it, and never treat a prediction as sign-off. 5. Read bridge_get_tree before any irreversible step: it carries the answers people gave, the follow-up questions they added for the next level (adopt them with bridge_add_node adopt=...; one they marked required must be adopted, and the task cannot finish until it is answered), nodes whose parent was answered after they were written, and nodes that need review because an answer they leaned on was corrected. When a node waits on a person, do the independent work first, then bridge_wait (it returns when a person acts, or at the timeout with who is still being waited on) rather than polling or giving up; people answer in Slack or the inbox, minutes or hours later, and the answer is on the tree whenever you read it. If your session restarts, bridge_start_task with the same client_key returns the same task. 6. bridge_finish_task when done; it is refused while a node waits on a person, or while a person has acted on the task since you last read the tree, and names which. Submit the complete diff against the intended base, including staged, unstaged and new files; plain git diff omits untracked files. Capture the patch once, read it as UTF-8 without newline conversion, and serialize it directly, preserving exact bytes and the final newline. Do not trim it, reconstruct it, or use shell command substitution that removes trailing newlines. Compute diff_sha256 from the original patch bytes before serialization and pass it with diff so Raven can reject transport damage before finishing. A matching host-reported hash is not independent attestation of the repository or tests. If the advisory review is running, use a whole-task bridge_wait to read its result, then repeat bridge_finish_task with the same complete diff and checks to refresh the saved proof and call bridge_export_proof. Review findings remain advisory, never authorization or a test run.

tools.name: bridge_review_discovery
tools.description: After inspecting the code, send your investigation observations and paths before asking people. Raven challenges missing judgment and distinguishes code investigations from approval questions. Use phase=finish with the actual diff before finishing an engaged task. Address findings by calling again with review_id and dispositions; either link a decision on this task or state what you investigated and why no new judgment is needed. Suggestions never authorize anything.

observations.description: What you actually found, with code revision/path/line or record/version citations and uncertainty; up to 24000 characters

review_id.description: Existing review to address; omit observations and diff when supplying dispositions

retry.description: Retry an unavailable review by review_id using its saved observations and current evidence

tools.name: bridge_start_task
tools.description: Call this the moment a task is kicked off, before any work, passing the task as it was given to you in `goal` and not only a title of your own: Raven looks at the task with what it knows (the tree, MAINTAINERS and CODEOWNERS, git history and blame, prior decisions, what is pending) and returns a verdict, engage or pass, with its reason and a discovery digest (areas, people, listings, prior decisions, pending questions). Most tasks are trivial and get pass. A task whose words name no area, kicked off with no paths, gets unplaced: call again with the same title, repo and client_key once you know the files, passing them as paths, and Raven judges it then. Returns task_id: the canvas every later node is written to. Pass client_key (your own id for this kickoff) so a retry returns the same task instead of starting a second one.

task_id.description: Existing task ID to resume without changing its repository. To replace a mistaken repository scope, abandon that task and start without task_id using a new client_key.

title.description: The task as kicked off, one line

goal.description: The task as it was given to you, in the requester's own words and in full. Raven triages on this: a one-line title of your own is thinner than what you were asked, and passes tasks that would otherwise engage

repo.description: Repository identity as the organization knows it: owner/name (acme/platform) or the git URL. This is what Raven matches its map and its memory against, so a path to your working copy or a scratch directory finds nothing and the verdict reads no repository at all; bridge_list_owners names the ones it holds

requester.description: Who kicked the task off (name, email, or both): their usual approvers count, and nothing is routed back to them

paths.description: Files or directories the task will touch, comma separated (optional)

client_key.description: Your own id for this kickoff; the same key returns the same task on a retry (optional, recommended)

facts.description: What holds for the whole task as key=value pairs, comma separated (release=library-next, customer=globex), copied from the task or its tickets and never invented: every node inherits them unless it states its own. Repository conditions use the task’s canonical repository; a contradictory facts.repo is refused. Never copy missing business facts from history (optional)

tools.name: bridge_add_node
tools.description: Write one judgment or authorization choice to the canvas as a node under the decision it grew from (parent_id). Code or test observations belong in the genuine decision context with citations, not in separate approval nodes. Do not invent a node when no human judgment is needed. You break the task down, Raven does not. Raven resolves the node from memory and records where it can (status resolved: evidence with a citation, marked for a person's sign-off, not authorization), predicts from precedent or from an unsigned earlier answer (predicted, to confirm), routes it to the person the signals name (pending), or says it does not know (unrouted). Idempotent: the same client_ref, or the same question in the same scope on this tree, returns the existing node; the same question about other files or another named customer is a new node, linked as related. Changed facts on a retry are not applied: use bridge_correct_node_facts with the current revision. To take up a follow-up question a person added, pass adopt=<its node_id>.

question.description: One specific judgment or authorization choice, not a code-inspection question

context.description: Evidence, constraints, consequences, including static code/test findings with revision, path/line or record/version citations and uncertainty. Keep findings distinct from the requested judgment here; name the current customer, account, environment or case

parent_id.description: The actual decision this choice grew from, not a node created solely to hold a factual observation (optional for a root decision)

paths.description: Files or directories this decision is about, comma separated

options.description: Candidate answers separated by | (a comma stays inside its option), each saying what it leads to; at most 8 (optional)

category.description: Optional: definition, policy, data-source, rollout, compat, ux, ops. data-source is a choice about the authoritative source, not a nonblocking code-fact type; every category keeps the same approval requirements

client_ref.description: Your own id for this node, for idempotent retries

requester.description: Overrides the task's requester for this node

adopt.description: node_id of a suggested follow-up question to adopt

depends_on.description: Actual decision node ids whose authorization is a prerequisite to acting on this choice, comma separated. Put cited factual premises in context instead; do not create dependency nodes for an evidence-reading checklist (optional)

facts.description: Known current applicability facts for this decision as key=value pairs, comma separated (plan=enterprise, customer=globex); put code/test observations and citations in context. Business rule conditions need current stated facts, never inferred authority. Repository conditions use the task’s canonical repository, never a historical value; contradictory facts.repo is refused (optional)

tools.name: bridge_correct_node_facts
tools.description: Explicitly replace the complete current facts of an active unsigned agent-origin node. Supply the exact fact_revision you read and a correction_ref for idempotent retries. Omitted facts become unknown; task or historical customer/environment facts are never inherited. Reruns local deterministic applicability. Existing source pins, dependencies and review flags remain binding. A newly verified standing grant may authorize when automatic rules are enabled; otherwise fresh sign-off remains required. Signed, human-acted, standing-rule-authorized and completed nodes cannot be edited: request a human inbox correction or start a new task. Historical snapshots are preserved.

expected_revision.description: Exact current fact_revision returned by bridge_get_decision, bridge_get_tree or bridge_add_node; reread after any change

correction_ref.description: Your unique ID for this correction within this task. Identical retries return its committed receipt; never reuse for a different request.

facts.description: Complete replacement key=value snapshot, comma separated; empty text clears business facts. State only current known facts. Repository conditions use the task's canonical repository and conflicting facts.repo is rejected.

reason.description: Why the current fact snapshot is being corrected

tools.name: bridge_settle_node
tools.description: Record your proposed answer to a genuine decision and why, not a standalone code-inspection finding. An existing factual-looking node still needs its normal sign-off; settlement does not clear it. Optional source_evidence binds exact current records you read; prose citations do not create source links. Existing dependencies remain and stale ones need a person's current-source review. This supersedes a pending background model reading, but stays agent-origin, unsigned, and marked for sign-off. It is not authorization: prepare on it, do not ship on it; use bridge_wait for the person to approve.

answer.description: Your proposed answer, still requiring human approval

source_evidence.description: Optional additive exact current source pins from bridge_get_record, in this repository and selected task namespace. Existing source roles and decision dependencies are retained. Omit for an unsupported manual opinion; never invent pins or infer them from citation prose.

tools.name: bridge_get_tree
tools.description: Read the whole canvas: the verdict, every node nested under its parent with status (resolved, predicted, pending, unrouted, answered, duplicate, suggested), whether a person authorized it (authorized) or it still waits on one (blocking), the answers people gave, the follow-up questions they added for the next level (adopt them with bridge_add_node), nodes whose parent was answered after they were written, nodes that need review because an answer they leaned on was corrected, what each node depends on, the notes people added to the task, and what to do next. Read it before an irreversible step and whenever you would otherwise wait.

tools.name: bridge_wait
tools.description: Wait for human changes or a running advisory diff review instead of polling. After finishing a task, a whole-task wait also waits for its review and returns review.status plus the result; once terminal, repeat bridge_finish_task with the same complete diff and checks to refresh the saved proof before exporting. For people: blocks up to timeout seconds (default 300) until something on the task changes because a person acted (an answer landed, a sign-off, a correction, a hand-on, a follow-up question added, a node put in doubt) and returns what changed with the next step for each node; on timeout it names the nodes still waiting and on whom. Call it once your independent work is done. Nothing is lost by not waiting: an answer that lands meanwhile is on the tree when you read it. While it waits it sends a progress notification every 15 seconds to a client that asked for progress. Every call remains bounded by the MCP call budget (50 seconds by default); call again with since to continue waiting. If Raven stops or restarts while you wait, the wait answers at once with interrupted set: call it again in a few seconds, nothing is lost.

timeout.description: Seconds requested, capped at the MCP call budget (50 by default); call again with since to keep waiting

since.description: The observed_at of your last bridge_get_tree or bridge_wait: what people did since then is returned at once (optional, recommended)

tools.name: bridge_finish_task
tools.description: Close the task. Refused while a node still waits on a person: an open question, an answer nobody signed, a decision put in doubt by a correction, or a follow-up question a person marked required that you have not adopted. The refusal names the nodes. Pass checks with what you actually ran (tests, build, lint) and their outcome, and diff with the change you made: both are recorded as your claim beside the decisions people authorized. Preserve the complete patch exactly, including new files and its final newline; pass diff_sha256 computed from the original bytes to catch transport changes before completion. This host-reported hash is not independent attestation. Given a diff, a model reads each authorized decision against it and returns follows: for each one a verdict, the line of the diff each requirement was read at, any counterexample it found (a path through the change that does what was ruled out) and the code it depends on that the diff does not show. That is a model's reading of what you supplied, not a test and never an approval: report it as read, name every counterexample, and the finish is not refused on a departure. Finishing means every decision was authorized, never that the change does what was authorized. Reading the diff can take minutes. Every finish call answers within about 45 seconds, even when progress notifications are enabled, with review.status running if needed; the reading goes on and is kept. Use a whole-task bridge_wait or bridge_get_tree to read its result, then repeat bridge_finish_task with the same complete diff and checks to save the terminal review in a refreshed proof; completed reads are reused without another model call. A reading is about the signed answers it read: when one changes afterwards, the tree marks the review stale and names the decisions, and you call bridge_finish_task again with your current diff. On a task Raven engaged, a finish whose diff changes a file someone else decides, when nothing on the task was put to them, is refused and names the file: write what the change there settles as a node for them, or call again with uncovered giving one line per file on why it settles nothing.

status.description: completed (default), working, or abandoned to close a mistaken task

reason.description: Required explanation when status is abandoned

checks.description: What you ran and what it said: the test command and its result, the build, the lint, in a few lines. Recorded as your claim; the first 2000 characters are kept (optional)

diff.description: The complete unified diff against the intended base, including staged, unstaged and new files (plain git diff omits untracked files). Read the patch as UTF-8 and serialize it directly, preserving exact bytes, whitespace and the final newline; do not trim, summarize, reconstruct or use shell command substitution that removes trailing newlines. A source file without a final newline still has a line-terminated patch with a No newline at end of file marker. Raven reads the authorized decisions against what you supply, so an excerpt can hide a requirement you implemented (optional)

diff_sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 computed by the coding host from the complete original patch bytes before serialization: exactly 64 hexadecimal characters. Raven rejects a mismatch with the submitted diff encoded as UTF-8 before finishing. This checks transport consistency of a host-reported hash, not independent repository or test attestation (optional, recommended with diff)

uncovered.description: Only when a finish was refused for changed files whose decider was asked nothing: one line per file, `<path>: why the change there settles nothing`. A file whose change does settle something gets a node instead (optional)

tools.name: bridge_get_decision
tools.description: Read current decision state. Every mode starts with recorded_history: decision-local saved-state counts and latest exact-version pointers for recorded approvals, signed states and rule uses. These classify immutable saved states, not verified signatures, distinct approval actions or current permission; rule use is not a new human signature. Zero means no matching saved states on this decision, not proof no approval occurred here or elsewhere. Preserved unsigned answer/rationale cannot establish or erase recorded signoff or rule use. Summary adds bounded history and a separately paged recorded-approval/rule-use index. Follow pagination with the same decision_id and limit, and read relevant exact versions and linked decisions before claiming no approval or only one prior decision. *_preview and omitted_fields are incomplete evidence. version_id reads one complete immutable decision_versions snapshot, with current authorization separately labeled; it is not a signed/proof revision ID. detail=full adds the overview while preserving every field of the complete original record. options are proposals, not the signed answer: people may refine them or answer outside them. Summarize the recorded answer and rationale; do not claim it selected an original option unless the record supports that. While approval_pending, continue independent work and do not ship on the answer.

detail.description: Default summary is bounded. full preserves the complete former response with a leading recorded_history overview and can be large; cannot combine with limit/cursor.

version_id.description: Exact decision_versions ID from recorded_history, context_history or historical_approvals, belonging to this decision; never a signed revision or proof revision. Reads the complete saved snapshot; cannot combine with limit/cursor.

limit.description: Total compact history/index rows per page, default 10. Encoded content budget may return fewer.

cursor.description: pagination.next_cursor; repeat the same decision_id and limit. Restart if results changed.

tools.name: bridge_export_proof
tools.description: Retrieve the portable change-proof bundle saved by bridge_finish_task. Includes the complete submitted diff and its SHA-256, signed decision revisions, scope, attribution, citations and host-reported checks, plus a review-ready Markdown summary. bundle.payload.review is the immutable saved snapshot; top-level review is the current reading. review_comparison states their IDs and statuses separately. review_snapshot_current=false does not imply a new review ID or attempt, and current findings must not be attributed to the saved snapshot. For historical lookup, report both without rewriting history. When preparing an updated proof, wait if review_pending, then repeat bridge_finish_task with the same complete diff and checks if review_snapshot_current is false. The digest detects tampering but is not a human digital signature or proof that tests ran.

task_id.description: Completed task ID, previously finished with the complete diff

tools.name: bridge_search_decisions
tools.description: For retrospective approval audits, use mode=history to include relevant needs-review, withdrawn and superseded saved evidence; read exact versions and linked decisions before claiming no prior approval. Default mode=current finds similar approved or evidence-resolved decisions as evidence (stemmed lexical overlap, hashed cosine, FTS5, recency-weighted). standing_grant separately labels the current recorded reuse terms; answer/context/rationale preserve the original task. A later explicit grant can permit conditional reuse across work items. Search alone does not evaluate that permission: supply current facts on a scoped node and use its authorized/signoff result. Do not treat older task-only rationale as cancelling a later recorded grant, or infer missing business facts from history. options are proposals; the recorded human answer may refine them or fall outside them.

query.description: Question to search

mode.description: Default current preserves approved/evidence-resolved retrieval. Explicit history searches saved evidence including needs-review, withdrawn and superseded rows; never authorizes reuse.

limit.description: Historical mode only: bounded matches per page, default 10.

cursor.description: Historical mode only: pagination.next_cursor; repeat the same query, repo and limit.

tools.name: bridge_list_owners
tools.description: Discover contacts, teams, optional verified authority, configured owners and inferred ownership with bounded pages. Discovery is never approval: omitted or unmatched rows do not mean no owner or required approver. Follow pagination.next_cursor with the same arguments until has_more is false; if results change, discard prior pages and restart. Use bridge_add_node for actual routing and bridge_get_tree for signoff.

repo.description: Optional exact repository scope for ownership/authority, including global authority. Contacts, owners, teams and graph totals stay organization-wide.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive substring of displayed names, emails, handles, teams, paths, scopes or other row text, independently per list (at most 200 characters).

limit.description: Total rows across all lists per page, including graph.repos: 1 to 200, default 100. A 48 KiB JSON-encoded content budget may return fewer intact rows.

cursor.description: pagination.next_cursor from the previous page; repeat the same query, repo and limit. This is a position, never a credential or authority grant.

tools.name: bridge_ingest_repo
tools.description: Build or refresh the ownership map and record graph from a local git checkout (shared HTTP instances require an operator credential; ordinary agent credentials use the checkout ingested during setup): git log, blame shares, CODEOWNERS, Reviewed-by trailers, merged and squashed PRs.

path.description: Absolute path to a local git checkout

tools.name: bridge_import_record
tools.description: Import a ticket, document or Slack record retrieved through your connected tools. For an existing stored record, use bridge_lookup_record, bridge_get_record and bridge_link_work_item to attach task context without reimporting it. Copy the source accurately, including status, author and permalink. This is evidence and a routing signal, never human authorization. Do not import secrets, unrelated private records, or Slack Real-time Search results (they must stay transient).

kind.description: ticket, jira, issue, doc, slack or note; kinds retain separate identities

ref.description: Stable source identifier such as NET-102

author.description: Source author's email, Slack member ID or full name

status.description: Source status including Cancelled, Superseded or Won't Do

resolved.description: Source resolution flag, never Raven approval. False prevents settled evidence; open or unknown status also prevents it.

paths.description: Complete related-path snapshot, comma separated or array. Supplied replaces old paths, [] clears; omitted retains.

provider.description: github, jira, slack, generic; omitted keeps the separate legacy identity

namespace.description: Required with a provider: stable source installation/site or Slack workspace ID

external_id.description: Stable object/message ID within the source namespace; defaults to ref

updated_at.description: Source update timestamp in ISO format, not ingestion time

source_version.description: Opaque source revision token, if supplied by the source

source_sequence.description: Monotonic source event sequence as an integer string, only if the source provides ordering

availability.description: available, deleted, or inaccessible; loss invalidates supporting reliance

access_scope.description: Source-provided audience/access boundary metadata; not a permission grant

retrieval_mode.description: Durable selection only; transient or Slack realtime search results are rejected

task_id.description: Optional selected work-item/task anchor on the same repository, not inferred from client_key

anchor_role.description: work_item (default) or context; neither is an approval or blocking premise

tools.name: bridge_get_record
tools.description: Read a durable source's immutable versions in its repository. The current head is separate from versions cited by older decisions. Source text and status are evidence, never approval.

tools.name: bridge_link_work_item
tools.description: Explicitly link an existing record you read to an open task without reimporting it. Copy its exact current record/version and canonical identity from bridge_get_record; use bridge_lookup_record first to resolve external IDs or references and ambiguity. This creates only an additive task work_item/context association, visible on the tree and history; it never creates supporting evidence, signs a decision, grants approval, or removes earlier links. facts.work_item declares an ID but alone remains unlinked. Closed tasks retain their historical associations.

repo.description: Exact stored repository key matching the task

source_version_id.description: Exact current source_version_id read through bridge_get_record

provider.description: Canonical source provider

namespace.description: Canonical source installation/workspace namespace

external_id.description: Optional exact stable external ID; omit both external_id and ref to select by the exact record/version; never supply both

ref.description: Optional exact current display ref; omit both ref and external_id to select by the exact record/version; supplied ambiguous refs are refused

role.description: Defaults to work_item; both are context associations, never premises

tools.name: bridge_lookup_record
tools.description: Resolve an exact external work-item/source ID or current human-readable ref in one exact repository, without a prior import or an internal record_id. Optional provider, namespace and object_kind disambiguate installations and kinds. Ambiguity returns candidates, never a newest winner. Returns bounded metadata, observed versions and explicit typed task/decision links, without source bodies or URLs. Latest observed status is evidence, not adopted policy or approval.

repo.description: Exact stored repository key, not a path or URL

external_id.description: Exact stable external ID; supply this or ref, not both

ref.description: Exact current display ref; supply this or external_id, not both. Renamed old display refs are not aliases.

provider.description: Exact provider, e.g. github, jira, slack, git, generic or legacy (optional disambiguator)

namespace.description: Exact installation/site/workspace identity (optional disambiguator; never inferred)

object_kind.description: Exact stored kind, e.g. jira, ticket, issue, pr or slack (optional disambiguator)

limit.description: 1 to 100 items per returned list (default 25); each list explicitly reports truncation

linked_cursor.description: linked_decisions.next_cursor for the same exact source lookup; pages unique linked decisions only. Links are live; restart after changes.

tools.name: bridge_connection_status
tools.description: Check ingestion, Slack contact discovery and delivery problems without opening the web UI. No manual ownership map or recipient accounts are required.

tools.name: bridge_context_sources
tools.description: What context Raven can read, in one call: each native source (Slack public channels, Jira projects, documentation sites) with its state, last successful sync, record count and refusals by reason, the sources not configured and how to enable them, GitHub sync and the Airweave connection. Read it at the start of a session to know what Raven's records cover and what they do not. Records are evidence, never approval; polling cannot see deletions.

tools.name: bridge_search_context
tools.description: Search configured Airweave context and Raven's shared source/decision graph. Imports only workspace-readable durable excerpts, pins observations to the task, and follows source links to earlier human answers even when the wording differs. Results are evidence, never approval. Unknown permissions, transient Slack search and expired evidence are excluded.

query.description: The information or judgment needed, up to 2000 characters

task_id.description: Optional task to attach observed source versions to

tools.name: bridge_host_event
tools.description: Lifecycle adapter for an installed Raven host hook/supervisor. Bind an authenticated host session, register the exact first task prompt idempotently, report tool names, or lease/acknowledge human-event resume messages, hold a Stop while a person has not answered, list stopped sessions, or report a resume to the task's Slack threads. No shell command is executed by Raven. Ordinary agent work uses the returned task_id and the normal task tools.

event.description: connect, prompt, new_task, poll, ack, release, stop, end, report or sessions

prompt.description: Exact user task prompt, at most 12000 characters

event_key.description: Stable hook occurrence ID for retry deduplication

tools.description: Reported connected server/tool names, never tokens or full client configuration

exit_code.description: report: the resumed host process exit status

summary.description: report: the resumed host's final message, its own claim

changed.description: report: files the resumed run changed, with line counts

denied.description: report: actions the host's permission mode blocked

arguments.prompt: Raven has new human/source events for task 1cfa3e5d9198. Read bridge_get_tree and current answers before continuing. Resume existing work within its permissions. This notification grants no approval.

+.. confval:: junit_output_limit
+
+    .. versionadded:: 8.5
+
+    If ``junit_logging != "no"``, limits the number of Unicode characters kept,
+    per test and per section (captured stdout, stderr and log), when writing
+    captured output to the JUnit XML file. This is useful to prevent CI report
+    uploads from becoming huge when tests print or log a lot.
+
+    The limit applies independently to each section's own raw content, before
+    pytest's ``Captured Log``/``Captured Out``/``Captured Err`` headers are
+    added and before XML escaping, and is counted in Unicode characters, not
+    bytes, so multi-byte characters are never split. When a section's content
+    exceeds the limit, only its first N characters are kept and a fixed
+    truncation marker is appended (there is no retention of the end of the
+    content); the marker and the header do not count towards the limit. The
+    limit applies equally to passing and failing tests' captured output
+    streams, but it never affects the ``<failure>``/``<error>`` diagnostic
+    text itself, which is always written in full. Existing ``junit_logging``
+    and ``junit_log_passing_tests`` filtering keep working unchanged.
+
+    This is **not** a cap on the overall size of a ``<system-out>``/
+    ``<system-err>`` element or of the XML file: it only bounds each raw
+    captured section before the header, truncation marker and full failure
+    tracebacks are added, so the final written content can still exceed the
+    configured number of characters.
+
+    Default is ``0``, which disables truncation and keeps the full captured
+    output, preserving the behavior from previous pytest versions (zero means
+    unlimited). Setting it to a negative or non-integer value is a
+    configuration error. Opt in by setting it to a positive number of
+    characters:
+
+    .. code-block:: ini
+
+        [pytest]
+        junit_logging = all
+        junit_output_limit = 2000
+
+
 .. confval:: junit_suite_name
 
     To set the name of the root test suite xml item, you can configure the ``junit_suite_name`` option in your config file:

     return re.sub(illegal_xml_re, repl, str(arg))
 
 
+_TRUNCATION_MARKER = "\n[... output truncated ...]\n"
+
+
+def _truncate_content(content: str, limit: int) -> str:
+    """Truncate ``content`` to at most ``limit`` characters, keeping the start.
+
+    Operates on Unicode code points rather than bytes, so multi-byte
+    characters are never split. The appended marker does not count towards
+    ``limit``.
+    """
+    if limit <= 0 or len(content) <= limit:
+        return content
+    return content[:limit] + _TRUNCATION_MARKER
+
+
+def _parse_output_limit(value: str) -> int:
+    """Parse and validate the ``junit_output_limit`` ini value."""
+    try:
+        limit = int(value)
+    except ValueError:
+        raise pytest.UsageError(
+            f"junit_output_limit must be an integer, got {value!r}"
+        ) from None
+    if limit < 0:
+        raise pytest.UsageError(
+            f"junit_output_limit must be a non-negative integer, got {limit}"
+        )
+    return limit
+

+

+    If ``junit_logging != "no"``, limits the number of Unicode characters kept,
+    per test and per section (captured stdout, stderr and log), when writing
+    captured output to the JUnit XML file. This is useful to prevent CI report
+    uploads from becoming huge when tests print or log a lot.
+
+    The limit applies independently to each section's own raw content, before
+    pytest's ``Captured Log``/``Captured Out``/``Captured Err`` headers are
+    added and before XML escaping, and is counted in Unicode characters, not
+    bytes, so multi-byte characters are never split. When a section's content
+    exceeds the limit, only its first N characters are kept and a fixed
+    truncation marker is appended (there is no retention of the end of the
+    content); the marker and the header do not count towards the limit. The
+    limit applies equally to passing and failing tests' captured output
+    streams, but it never affects the ``<failure>``/``<error>`` diagnostic
+    text itself, which is always written in full. Existing ``junit_logging``

+    configured number of characters.

+Added a new :confval:`junit_output_limit` ini option (default ``0``, disabled) to limit how many Unicode characters of captured output (stdout, stderr, log) are kept per test and per section when writing the JUnit XML report. This helps avoid huge CI report uploads for test suites that print or log a lot.
+
+When enabled (e.g. ``junit_output_limit = 2000``), each raw captured section exceeding the limit is truncated to its first N Unicode characters (never splitting a multi-byte character) with a fixed truncation marker appended, before pytest's own headers are added -- this is a per-section character limit, not a byte or total file-size cap, so the header, marker and full failure tracebacks can still push the final written content past N characters. Truncation applies equally to passing and failing tests' captured output, and never affects the ``<failure>``/``<error>`` diagnostic text itself, which is always written in full. Existing ``junit_logging``/``junit_log_passing_tests`` filtering and configurations without this option (the default ``0`` means unlimited) are unaffected, as the feature is opt-in.

+        [pytest]
+        junit_logging=system-out
+        junit_output_limit=10
+        junit_family={xunit_family}
+    """
+    )
+    pytester.makepyfile(
+        """
+        import sys
+
+        def test_func():
+            sys.stdout.write("x" * 1000)
+            assert False, "y" * 1000
+    """
+    )
+    result, dom = run_and_parse(family=xunit_family)
+    assert result.ret == 1
+    node = dom.get_first_by_tag("testcase")
+
+    system_out = node.get_first_by_tag("system-out")
+    assert "x" * 10 + "\n[... output truncated ...]\n" in system_out.text
+    assert "x" * 11 not in system_out.text
+
+    failure = node.get_first_by_tag("failure")
+    assert "y" * 1000 in failure.text
+    assert "truncated" not in failure.text
+
+
+def test_junit_output_limit_unicode(
+    pytester: Pytester, run_and_parse: RunAndParse
+) -> None:
+    """Truncation operates on Unicode code points, never splitting a
+    multi-byte character."""
+    pytester.makeini(
+        """
+        [pytest]
+        junit_logging=system-out
+        junit_output_limit=20
+    """
+    )
+    pytester.makepyfile(
+        """
+        # -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+        def test_func():
+            print("é" * 100)
+    """
+    )
+    result, dom = run_and_parse()
+    assert result.ret == 0
+    node = dom.get_first_by_tag("testcase")
+    system_out = node.get_first_by_tag("system-out")
+    assert "é" * 20 + "\n[... output truncated ...]\n" in system_out.text
+    assert "é" * 21 not in system_out.text
+    # No mangled byte of the "é" UTF-8 encoding anywhere in the output.
+    import string
+
+    allowed = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " \n"
+    for ch in system_out.text:
+        assert ch == "é" or ch in allowed
+
+
+def test_junit_output_limit_rejects_non_integer(pytester: Pytester) -> None:
+    pytester.makeini(
+        """
+        [pytest]
+        junit_output_limit=not-a-number
+    """
+    )
+    pytester.makepyfile("def test_func(): pass")
+    xml_path = pytester.path.joinpath("junit.xml")
+    result = pytester.runpytest(f"--junitxml={xml_path}")
+    assert result.ret == pytest.ExitCode.USAGE_ERROR
+    result.stderr.fnmatch_lines(
+        ["*junit_output_limit must be an integer, got 'not-a-number'*"]
+    )
+
+
+def test_junit_output_limit_rejects_negative(pytester: Pytester) -> None:
+    pytester.makeini(
+        """
+        [pytest]
+        junit_output_limit=-1
+    """
+    )
+    pytester.makepyfile("def test_func(): pass")
+    xml_path = pytester.path.joinpath("junit.xml")
+    result = pytester.runpytest(f"--junitxml={xml_path}")
+    assert result.ret == pytest.ExitCode.USAGE_ERROR
+    result.stderr.fnmatch_lines(
+        ["*junit_output_limit must be a non-negative integer, got -1*"]
+    )
+

+Added a new :confval:`junit_output_limit` ini option (default ``0``, disabled) to limit how many Unicode characters of captured output (stdout, stderr, log) are kept per test and per section when writing the JUnit XML report. This helps avoid huge CI report uploads for test suites that print or log a lot.
+
+When enabled (e.g. ``junit_output_limit = 2000``), each raw captured section exceeding the limit is truncated to its first N Unicode characters (never splitting a multi-byte character) with a fixed truncation marker appended, before pytest's own headers are added -- this is a per-section character limit, not a byte or total file-size cap, so the header, marker and full failure tracebacks can still push the final written content past N characters. Truncation applies equally to passing and failing tests' captured output, and never affects the ``<failure>``/``<error>`` diagnostic text itself, which is always written in full. Existing ``junit_logging``/``junit_log_passing_tests`` filtering and configurations without this option (the default ``0`` means unlimited) are unaffected, as the feature is opt-in.

+.. confval:: junit_output_limit
+
+    .. versionadded:: 8.5
+
+    If ``junit_logging != "no"``, limits the number of Unicode characters kept,
+    per test and per section (captured stdout, stderr and log), when writing
+    captured output to the JUnit XML file. This is useful to prevent CI report
+    uploads from becoming huge when tests print or log a lot.
+
+    The limit applies independently to each section's own raw content, before
+    pytest's ``Captured Log``/``Captured Out``/``Captured Err`` headers are
+    added and before XML escaping, and is counted in Unicode characters, not
+    bytes, so multi-byte characters are never split. When a section's content
+    exceeds the limit, only its first N characters are kept and a fixed
+    truncation marker is appended (there is no retention of the end of the
+    content); the marker and the header do not count towards the limit. The
+    limit applies equally to passing and failing tests' captured output
+    streams, but it never affects the ``<failure>``/``<error>`` diagnostic
+    text itself, which is always written in full. Existing ``junit_logging``
+    and ``junit_log_passing_tests`` filtering keep working unchanged.
+
+    This is **not** a cap on the overall size of a ``<system-out>``/
+    ``<system-err>`` element or of the XML file: it only bounds each raw
+    captured section before the header, truncation marker and full failure
+    tracebacks are added, so the final written content can still exceed the
+    configured number of characters.
+
+    Default is ``0``, which disables truncation and keeps the full captured
+    output, preserving the behavior from previous pytest versions (zero means
+    unlimited). Setting it to a negative or non-integer value is a
+    configuration error. Opt in by setting it to a positive number of
+    characters:
+

+

+Added a new :confval:`junit_output_limit` ini option (default ``0``, disabled) to limit how many Unicode characters of captured output (stdout, stderr, log) are kept per test and per section when writing the JUnit XML report. This helps avoid huge CI report uploads for test suites that print or log a lot.
+
+When enabled (e.g. ``junit_output_limit = 2000``), each raw captured section exceeding the limit is truncated to its first N Unicode characters (never splitting a multi-byte character) with a fixed truncation marker appended, before pytest's own headers are added -- this is a per-section character limit, not a byte or total file-size cap, so the header, marker and full failure tracebacks can still push the final written content past N characters. Truncation applies equally to passing and failing tests' captured output, and never affects the ``<failure>``/``<error>`` diagnostic text itself, which is always written in full. Existing ``junit_logging``/``junit_log_passing_tests`` filtering and configurations without this option (the default ``0`` means unlimited) are unaffected, as the feature is opt-in.

         junit_log_passing_tests = False
 
 
+.. confval:: junit_output_limit
+
+    .. versionadded:: 8.5
+
+    If ``junit_logging != "no"``, limits the number of Unicode characters kept,
+    per test and per section (captured stdout, stderr and log), when writing
+    captured output to the JUnit XML file. This is useful to prevent CI report
+    uploads from becoming huge when tests print or log a lot.
+
+    The limit applies independently to each section's own raw content, before
+    pytest's ``Captured Log``/``Captured Out``/``Captured Err`` headers are
+    added and before XML escaping, and is counted in Unicode characters, not
+    bytes, so multi-byte characters are never split. When a section's content
+    exceeds the limit, only its first N characters are kept and a fixed
+    truncation marker is appended (there is no retention of the end of the
+    content); the marker and the header do not count towards the limit. The
+    limit applies equally to passing and failing tests' captured output
+    streams, but it never affects the ``<failure>``/``<error>`` diagnostic
+    text itself, which is always written in full. Existing ``junit_logging``
+    and ``junit_log_passing_tests`` filtering keep working unchanged.
+
+    This is **not** a cap on the overall size of a ``<system-out>``/
+    ``<system-err>`` element or of the XML file: it only bounds each raw
+    captured section before the header, truncation marker and full failure
+    tracebacks are added, so the final written content can still exceed the
+    configured number of characters.
+
+    Default is ``0``, which disables truncation and keeps the full captured
+    output, preserving the behavior from previous pytest versions (zero means
+    unlimited). Setting it to a negative or non-integer value is a
+    configuration error. Opt in by setting it to a positive number of
+    characters:
+
+    .. code-block:: ini
+
+        [pytest]
+        junit_logging = all
+        junit_output_limit = 2000
+
+
 .. confval:: junit_suite_name
 
     To set the name of the root test suite xml item, you can configure the ``junit_suite_name`` option in your config file:
@@ -2389,6 +2429,16 @@ All the command-line flags can be obtained by running ``pytest --help``::
                             Duration time to report: one of total|call
       junit_family (string):
                             Emit XML for schema: one of legacy|xunit1|xunit2
+      junit_output_limit (string):
+                            Maximum number of Unicode characters to keep, per
+                            test and per section (captured stdout, stderr,
+                            log), when writing captured output to the JUnit
+                            report. Longer output is truncated, keeping only
+                            the start and appending a truncation marker. Does
+                            not affect the <failure>/<error> diagnostic text

+                            and keep the full output, preserving previous

+Added a new :confval:`junit_output_limit` ini option (default ``0``, disabled) to limit how many Unicode characters of captured output (stdout, stderr, log) are kept per test and per section when writing the JUnit XML report. This helps avoid huge CI report uploads for test suites that print or log a lot.
+
+When enabled (e.g. ``junit_output_limit = 2000``), each raw captured section exceeding the limit is truncated to its first N Unicode characters (never splitting a multi-byte character) with a fixed truncation marker appended, before pytest's own headers are added -- this is a per-section character limit, not a byte or total file-size cap, so the header, marker and full failure tracebacks can still push the final written content past N characters. Truncation applies equally to passing and failing tests' captured output, and never affects the ``<failure>``/``<error>`` diagnostic text itself, which is always written in full. Existing ``junit_logging``/``junit_log_passing_tests`` filtering and configurations without this option (the default ``0`` means unlimited) are unaffected, as the feature is opt-in.
